```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(meddecide)
```

This article shows the two basic diagnostic-accuracy analyses:

- **Medical Decision** (`decision()`, **meddecide > Decision**) works from raw data:
  one column for the reference standard, one for the test.
- **Medical Decision Calculator** (`decisioncalculator()`,
  **meddecide > Decision Calculators**) works from the four cell counts.

## From raw data: `decision()`

A tiny example file ships with the package.

```{r data}
df_dec <- read.csv(system.file("extdata", "decision_example.csv", package = "meddecide"))
df_dec$gold    <- factor(df_dec$gold)
df_dec$newtest <- factor(df_dec$newtest)
str(df_dec)
```

Columns are passed **by name**. Name the positive *and* the negative level of
both the reference standard and the test; all four are required, so the analysis
never guesses which level means "disease".

```{r decision}
res <- decision(
  data = df_dec,
  gold = "gold",
  goldPositive = "1",
  goldNegative = "0",
  newtest = "newtest",
  testPositive = "1",
  testNegative = "0",
  ci = TRUE
)
res$cTable$asDF      # 2 x 2 table
res$ratioTable$asDF  # sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV, likelihood ratios
res$epirTable_ratio$asDF  # sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV with 95% CIs (ci = TRUE)
```

With only 10 cases the confidence intervals are very wide; the example only shows
the mechanics.

## From counts: `decisioncalculator()`

```{r calculator, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 5}
calc <- decisioncalculator(TP = 90, FN = 10, TN = 80, FP = 20,
                           ci = TRUE, fagan = TRUE)
calc$epirTable_ratio$asDF  # estimates with 95% confidence intervals
calc$plot1           # Fagan nomogram
```

The Fagan nomogram shows how a positive or negative result moves a pre-test
probability to a post-test probability through the likelihood ratios. By default
the pre-test probability is the prevalence in the table; set `pp = TRUE` and
`pprob` to use a prevalence from your own population.
